root_cause.text: In `ip6_err_gen_icmpv6_unreach()`, the skb control block (`cb`) from an outer IPv4 ICMP error packet is not cleared when cloning, so `icmp6_send()` interprets the leftover IPv4 `inet_skb_parm` as an IPv6 `inet6_skb_parm`, allowing an attacker to control the `dsthao` field and trigger an out-of-bounds read and write in `mip6_addr_swap()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explains that "the cipso offset in inet_skb_parm.opt directly overlaps with dsthao in inet6_skb_parm at offset 18" and that an attacker can send a forged ICMPv4 error with a CIPSO IP option to set `dsthao` to a non-zero value, which is then used as an offset in `ipv6_find_tlv()`. The patch adds `memset(IP6CB(skb2), 0, sizeof(*IP6CB(skb2)));` to clear the inherited IPv4 control block data.

intent_record.what: Added memset to zero out the IP6CB (IPv6 control block) on a cloned skb, along with a comment explaining it removes debris left by the IPv4 stack.
intent_record.how: By zeroing the IP6CB structure, any leftover packet control information from a previous IPv4 path is cleared, ensuring that subsequent IPv6 processing does not misinterpret stale data when generating ICMPv6 unreachable messages.
